I didn't realize how useful Google Contacts was until I used these 5 features

I was missing out on some of the app's best features.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:30 AM ET

•

•

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

Google Contacts is an app that I’ve simultaneously used and ignored for years. It’s always on my device because I use it to sync phone numbers and email addresses to my Google Account so that I always have a backup, but I’d rarely explored its distinct features until recently. That’s when I realized just how much you can do in the app.

In particular, several features have turned the app into a powerful way for me to manage contact information.

Readers' poll

Which Google Contacts feature do you like the most?

22 votes

Weather and time info

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

I didn’t realize that Google Contacts had this feature until I was trying out ways to replicate Pixel VIPs on other devices. If you have an address saved for a person, their page in the Google Contacts app will update with their local time and weather. This works even if you just have a suburb saved for the contact — so you don’t have to add their exact home location.

This feature works particularly well for contacts who live in another time zone or people you visit often. For example, by having my brother’s suburb in Ireland saved, I can double-check the time there before messaging him without having to use a time zone calculator or figure out whether Ireland is currently on summer time.

This feature is great for contacts who live in different time zones or areas with a different climate.

Meanwhile, for friends who live in other parts of Cape Town, I can check whether I need to bring a coat before I visit them since the weather can be wildly different depending on where you live in the city. This is especially true when it comes to wind and rain.

To add an address for a contact, follow these steps:

1. Open a contact’s page by tapping their name in the app

2. Tap the pen icon. Scroll down and select Address.

3. Type in their location and then select Save.

4. After some time, the location field will update with the weather and time information. If it’s not updating, tap on the arrow icon to open Google Maps and exit again, and the field should update.

Birthday and important date reminders

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Besides the birthdays I’ve known since childhood, keeping track of important dates and anniversaries is difficult for me. For a long time, I relied on Facebook to notify me when it is a friend’s birthday. But as I use the social media site less, and people I know delete their accounts, this method hasn’t been reliable.

That’s why I was glad to find out that I can add birthdays and important date reminders to Google Contacts. These dates also sync with my Google Calendar, adding a bit of redundancy for extra reassurance that I don’t miss an important date.

With this feature, I don't have to rely on Facebook to remember the birthdays of important contacts.

This feature requires you to save the contact to your Google Account and you need to add the notification at least 24 hours before the date. You also need to enable notifications in the Google Contacts app. The feature lets you choose the day you receive the notification from a range of options.

To add a birthday or important date for a contact:

1. Open the contact page and select Reminders.

2. Select New reminder.

3. Choose the type of reminder from the available labels (Birthday, Anniversary, or Custom) and then choose the date.

4. Set the date and time you want to receive your reminder. Then, select Save.

5. You will see a small message box that notes that the reminder has been saved.

Notes

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Many of us will be familiar with the habit of adding descriptive terms to a contact’s name so that you remember who they are. I have countless contacts with words like “neighbor,” “courier,” “landlord,” or the company where they work added to the name in brackets. But the Notes feature in Google Contacts means that you can keep the contact name tidy without a bunch of terms added after their actual name.

The Notes field is also helpful for general notes about a contact, and it’s one of the fields that Pixel VIPs surfaces. You can use it to add gift ideas, remember your friend’s favorite color, or write down any other useful information. You don’t have to rely on your memory.

Notes provide a helpful place to jot down important details you want to remember about your contact.

This will also make it easier when it comes time to clean up your contacts, since you can easily figure out if you still need to message that person in the future. For example, there have been a few times I’ve needed to take down the number of a company driver when I’m at a press event. These contacts are only relevant for one day, yet they stay in the app years later.

To add a note to a contact:

1. Tap the pen icon on a contact page.

2. Scroll down to the Notes field.

3. Type in the details you want to add and tap on Save.

4. You will now be able to see notes on their page below their main contact details.

Custom field

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

At first, I figured that Custom field simply duplicates what Notes can do in Google Contacts. But I realized pretty quickly that the Notes section can become cluttered if you depend on it significantly. That’s where the Custom field feature comes in handy. It allows you to add more information to a contact’s page in a structured way, without creating a long wall of text. It also prioritizes this information at the top of the page, along with their contact details.

This works best for fields that you want to repeat across different contacts. For example, you might want to save social media pages for business contacts depending on your industry, or you may just want to remember how you met someone. Custom fields are specifically there to fill in the gaps that other fields like Website, Job title, and Related people don’t cover.

A Custom field lets you add extra information to your contact that displays near the top of their profile.

For example, for neighbors, I can use the custom field feature to list which unit they live in within my complex. For friends that I know from online games, I can add their gamer tag if I don’t want to save it as their nickname. Because you determine the title of the field and the text included, the possibilities are endless.

To create a custom field for a contact:

1. Select the pen icon on their contact page to edit their profile.

2. Scroll down and select Other > Custom field.

3. Add the title in Custom field and the label in Custom label. Then tap Save.

4. The Custom field will now appear below their contact details on their profile.

Your info

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Google Contacts is perfect for saving the contact information of others, but you can also use it to edit and share your own. I find this more convenient than trying to edit my details using the Google Account personal info page, especially since it’s right at the top of the Google Contacts app. It’s also specifically focused on information that you want to share with others, rather than information Google has about you.

On the Your info page, you can change your profile picture (which will be visible to others), add contact details like your phone and email, and add additional information like your address and certain fields. These fields aren’t as extensive as those available for your saved contacts. You can add Company, Department, Job title, and Website. However, you can also add your nickname when you edit your display name.

The Your info page makes it easy to share your details with someone else, using methods like Quick Share.

You can then use the sharing feature to share your details with others. Google Contacts allows you to select which details you choose to share, which is particularly helpful. You can share these details using Quick Share or a messaging app. The recipient can then open these details in their own contacts app.

To edit your details in the Your info page, simply use the pen icon. If you want to share your details with someone else:

1. Tap the Share icon.

2. Select the details you want to share by selecting Choose details to share, and then tap Share.

3. Select the sharing method for your contact file.

After diving into these Google Contacts features, I realized that there’s a lot more going on in the app than I expected. Over the years, the app has become more feature-rich, even including shortcuts to features like location sharing and navigation.

The features I’ve discussed stand out in particular because they’ve changed the way I view the app. If you haven’t tried them, I recommend checking them out to see how you can put them to use.

items.title: Apple, Samsung, and other phone makers don’t think they can sell as many phones in 2027
items.summary: The smartphone market is bracing for troubled times ahead.
items.body:

Mobile

Apple, Samsung, and other phone makers don’t think they can sell as many phones in 2027

The smartphone market is bracing for troubled times ahead.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:11 AM ET

•

•

Robert Triggs / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Most major phone makers have reportedly lowered their 2027 shipment targets due to rising memory costs.

• Xiaomi and vivo are cutting the most, by 25% and 29% respectively, while Apple and Samsung are also reducing their targets.

• HONOR is the only major phone brand that’s not reducing its shipment target for 2027.

The memory shortage has been a theme throughout this year, and we’ve seen several manufacturers hike phone prices because of it. Now, it seems to be hitting manufacturers’ sales plans as well.

According to a report from Jiemian News, citing supply chain sources, most major smartphone makers have finalized their shipment targets for 2027 and expect to sell considerably fewer phones next year.

The steepest cuts are reportedly coming from vivo and Xiaomi, going from 85 million units in 2026 to 60 million in 2027 for vivo and from 120 million down to 90 million in 2027 for Xiaomi. That’s a reduction of 29% and 25%, respectively. Motorola is aiming for 40 million unit sales next year, down 20% from 50 million in 2026. OPPO has also reportedly finalized a target of 90 million units — a 14% drop from its 2026 sales target.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Meanwhile, Samsung and Apple are cutting less. The South Korean giant is reportedly aiming for 210 million units, down 9.5% from 232 million, while Apple is dropping 5.6% from 233 million to 220 million units.

The only exception, according to the report, is HONOR. It’s reportedly sticking with 50 million units for 2027, the same as this year. At the HONOR 700 series launch, CEO Li Jian said that mid-range phones face bigger cost pressures than flagships, and that HONOR plans to keep pushing while others pull back. These higher cost pressures, coupled with price hikes, also made flagship phones look like a better deal than mid-range phones, and they became more popular this year. The report also cites IDC data showing that HONOR was the only leading Chinese phone brand to grow shipments quarter-on-quarter in Q3.

Stephen Schenck / Android Authority

Li Jian also said some phones have been downgraded in chips, cameras, or memory to hold prices steady as the memory shortage worsens and prices skyrocket. In fact, a recent Counterpoint report stated that DRAM revenue in Q3 2026 approached $200 billion, growing 369% year-on-year due to AI server demand.

Smartphone shipments throughout 2026 have been on a rough-and-tumble ride. Earlier this year, companies like Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo reported double-digit declines in sales due to rising memory costs.

It seems 2027 will bring more of the same, with only HONOR holding out some hope for its portfolio. Meanwhile, the memory shortage is expected to continue into 2028, according to the report. Any reprieve from heavily inflated prices and dwindling sales is expected only toward the end of 2027 or in early 2028.

Survey says nearly 3 in 5 readers are already on Android 17, despite low global numbers

That still leaves plenty of devices stuck on older versions, though.

•

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

It’s been several months since Android 17 made its mainstream debut, but as of October 2026, a tiny percentage of devices were running it. As is so often the case, it takes a while for the latest version of Google’s mobile OS to proliferate across devices, but it’s particularly worrying that nearly four months after launch, just 1% of devices were running it.

We just had to know if these broader Android Studio figures matched those of our readers. So, we ran a poll, asking readers which Android version their device is running. The results are in, and it’s a completely different story.

4. My phone isn't running Android.19 votes2.2%

5. I'm unsure.6 votes0.7%

870 votes · androidauthority.com · results as of November 25, 2026

Nearly three in every five devices (58.2%) are running Android 17, which is certainly a stark difference from the 1% indicated by Android Studio in October. This suggests Google’s and other manufacturers’ update rollouts are progressing well, and that Android Authority readers are generally running devices that are either brand new or still on their extended software update plans.

Android 16 accounts for 15.5% of polled readers’ devices, and was the only other version to receive double-digit support. Android 15, 14, and 13 followed closely behind and are running on 13.4% of devices combined.

What’s particularly interesting is that Android 10 or older (3.9%) accounts for more devices than Android 11 (3.4%) or Android 12 (2.6%) individually.

There are a few things to note about this particular poll. One, it’s safe to say that the majority of Android Authority readers are enthusiasts, and therefore are more likely to be running bleeding-edge software where possible. Secondly, it ran for several weeks after we reported the initial Android Studio numbers from October 2026. This gap likely allowed for more devices to receive their Android 17 update, further skewing the results slightly.

Have you received the Android 17 update on your device yet? If not, what Android version is your device running? Let us know in the comments below.

items.title: Gemini Notebook’s flashcards just got a lot better for studies with three new features
items.summary: Your flashcards now have a better sense of time than you.

General technology

Gemini Notebook's flashcards just got a lot better for studies with three new features

Your flashcards now have a better sense of time than you.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 3:30 AM ET

•

•

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Gemini Notebook can now incorporate images from uploaded study materials into flashcards, making visual learning easier.

• Google has added an optional stopwatch to flashcard review sessions to help users practice recalling information under time pressure.

• You can now schedule flashcard review reminders through the Gemini mobile app, and all three improvements are available without a paid subscription.

Google has been adding some interesting features to Gemini Notebook lately. Just a few days ago, we reported that the tool could turn your research materials into interactive websites. Now, Google is improving the flashcard experience with three new features that could make studying more effective and, perhaps more importantly, easier to keep up with.

The first change addresses a limitation of text-based flashcards. Gemini Notebook can now pull relevant images from your uploaded study materials and incorporate them into flashcards. This should be handy for subjects where visual references matter. For instance, if you’re studying human anatomy, identifying different parts of the heart from a diagram could be much more effective than memorizing their names from a wall of text.

Another addition is an optional stopwatch that lets you time your flashcard review sessions. Remembering the correct answer is one thing, but recalling it quickly in an exam hall is another. For example, you could challenge yourself to work through a deck of flashcards in five minutes and gradually see how much faster you get with repeated practice.

Gemini’s floating overlay now helps you compare prices, check warranty terms across shopping apps

Gemini overlay uses screen context and recommends actions while using shopping apps on Android.

TL;DR

• Gemini’s floating overlay on Android now uses screen context to find the best shopping deals across apps.

• You can ask it to check if a product is worth considering or compare prices across different apps.

• The feature works by grabbing a screenshot of the page behind it but doesn’t require you to share your screen with Gemini Live.

Google already curates products from multiple online stores in the Shopping section of its search results. If you’d rather skip manually scouring products, you can ask Gemini or Google’s AI Mode to recommend or filter them based on your preferences. Now, Google is making these insights even more accessible with prompts on top of any popular shopping app on your phone.

Google is starting to roll out new shopping help prompts right via the Gemini overlay. When you open Gemini over a product page on a shopping app, it will now suggest prompts such as “Help me pick,” “Compare prices,” or “Check warranty and returns.” Tapping any prompt makes Gemini take a screenshot of the product page and use it as context along with the text prompt. For instance, when you ask it to compare prices, it will compare the current listing, say Amazon, against other online retailers, such as Walmart and Target, which can be useful for holiday shopping, especially for the ongoing Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales.

The ability to analyze your screen isn’t at all new for Gemini — the feature has been around for over two years. Last December, Google also expanded Gemini’s ability to scan what’s on your screen to deliver better results, even without you having to share your screen with Gemini Live. However, this is the first time we’re noticing shopping-specific contextual suggestions.

Gemini overlay uses a more verbose versions of these suggestions to prompt itself in chat. All of these conversations also appear in your Gemini chat history, and you can revisit them later.

That said, unlike PDFs, web pages, or YouTube videos, where Gemini can scan the entire media, shopping context will be limited to what’s visible on the screen and not what you would see when you scroll the page. Google has yet to update its support page for ways Gemini helps with shopping, but we anticipate the feature will work across multiple different shopping apps. We can confirm it works with Amazon, Flipkart, and even quick commerce apps such as Blinkit.

The feature is already live with version 17.78.13 of the Google app and is likely part of a server-side rollout.

Another feature arriving with the latest version is the ability to mute Gemini Live’s voice output and get written responses (through captions) without having to type themselves. This lets users continue having verbal conversations with Gemini Live without disturbing others nearby, all without muting their mic or turning down the phone’s volume. We discovered this feature last month when we also found out about Google’s new, dazzling Gemini Live UI, but that has yet to go live.

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

To mute Gemini’s responses during a Live chat, you can tap the speaker icon in the top-right corner of the screen.

Mobile

Samsung promises One UI 9.5 will fix rapidly declining battery health on Galaxy phones

Premature battery wear or a software error?

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 3:09 AM ET

•

•

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Some Galaxy users have reported unusually rapid drops in battery health following the One UI 9.0 update.

• Samsung support says the upcoming One UI 9.5 update will address the issue.

• It’s unclear whether the problem stems from inaccurate battery health readings or accelerated battery degradation.

Battery life has been a sore point for some Galaxy owners since Samsung rolled out One UI 9.0, with users reporting increased battery drain on the Galaxy S24 and S25 series. But another battery-related concern has emerged following the update: unusually rapid drops in reported battery health. Luckily, Samsung support now says the upcoming One UI 9.5 update will address the issue.

In a post on Samsung’s Turkish community forum, a Galaxy user shared a response they received after submitting an error report through Samsung Members. The support representative explicitly stated that the battery health deterioration issue would be addressed with One UI 9.5. Here’s a Google Translate version:

The issue of decreased battery health you’re experiencing will be addressed with the upcoming One UI 9.5 update.

According to the user, battery health percentages have been dropping abnormally since the One UI 9.0 update, with some devices reportedly showing 94% battery health after just a month of use. The response came approximately two weeks after the user submitted their error report.

Alfatürk / Samsung Turkey community

Samsung introduced detailed battery health information with the Galaxy S25 series, giving owners more insight into how their batteries age. However, that information is only useful if the figures are accurate.

What’s unclear from Samsung’s response is whether One UI 9.0 is causing batteries to degrade faster than expected or whether there’s a software bug causing phones to underestimate their remaining battery capacity. While One UI 9.5 could correct inaccurate readings or address software issues contributing to premature battery wear, no software update can restore battery capacity that has already been physically lost.

The good news is that One UI 9.5 is already in beta, with the stable version expected to debut alongside the Galaxy S27 series in a couple of months. Granted, Galaxy owners experiencing abnormal drops in battery health may not have to wait much longer for a fix.

TL;DR

• A new leak has given us a look at the expected design and specs of the OnePlus Nord 7.

• The Nord 7 could come with an RGB light bar on the back and a dual-camera setup.

• It could also feature the Dimensity 8500 chipset, a 9,000mAh battery, and 80W fast charging support.

The OnePlus Nord 6 launched earlier this year, and we’re already seeing leaked images of the next phone in the lineup: the OnePlus Nord 7. This time, it seems OnePlus might be taking a slightly different approach for its Nord series.

Tipster Abhishek Aggarwal shared leaked images and specifications of the upcoming OnePlus Nord 7 in an X post. The most noticeable feature in the images is a light bar in the camera module, which could offer features similar to those seen on Nothing’s smartphones or the Pixel HiLight.

yabhishekhd / X

The images also show off a dual-camera setup. While we don’t know the exact camera specs OnePlus could use, hopefully it won’t be a downgrade over the 50MP primary and 8MP ultrawide-angle cameras that shipped on the OnePlus Nord 6 earlier this year. We can also see a punch-hole camera on the front.

The tipster also shared leaked specifications for the Nord 7. The phone could come with a Dimensity 8500 chipset and an AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate. The Nord 6, on the other hand, uses a Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chipset and an AMOLED display with a 165Hz refresh rate. Although the Dimensity 8500 is likely to offer similar performance, the 144Hz refresh rate would be a definite downgrade from the OnePlus Nord 6. The OnePlus Nord 7 could also come with a 9,000mAh battery — the same as the Nord 6 — with support for 80W fast charging.

It’s worth noting that OnePlus usually rebrands its Turbo series from China as the Nord series globally. It did that with the Nord 6, which was a rebranded OnePlus Turbo 6, and it was expected to do the same with the Nord 7. However, leaks suggest the OnePlus Turbo 7 will feature a Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 processor, a 200MP primary camera, a 185Hz display, and a battery close to 10,000mAh.

It’s possible that OnePlus is deviating from its strategy of launching its Turbo lineup globally as the Nord lineup. However, it’s also possible (and more probable) that one of the leaks surrounding the OnePlus Nord 7 or the OnePlus Turbo 7 is incorrect. The OnePlus Turbo 7 is expected to launch in China in December, and the Nord 7 could launch early next year, so we shouldn’t have to wait long for more concrete information on the specs for both phones.

Finally, someone who texts you first and brings good news.

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Google Discover

TL;DR

• The latest Google Messages beta integrates Gemini Tasks through the app’s existing floating Gemini button.

• Gemini can now proactively text you price-drop alerts, package delivery updates, subscription reminders, and daily briefings.

• The integration is currently limited to US users and requires Tasks to be enabled in the Gemini app.

Google recently made Gemini Tasks available to free users in six countries, including the US, Canada, and India. The company also introduced a feature called Channels, which lets you communicate with Gemini via text messages and email instead of opening the Gemini app every time you need something. Now, that experience is making its way to Google Messages.

According to 9to5Google, the latest Google Messages beta (version 20261120_01_RC00) has repurposed the app’s floating Gemini button. Tapping it now takes you to the Gemini Channels website, where you can set up the integration. Once that’s done, the button opens a conversation with Gemini within Google Messages. The integration relies on RCS Business Messaging.

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

What’s particularly exciting is that Gemini can text you first. Say you’re planning a vacation and want to track flight prices, or you’ve been waiting for a particular product to go on sale. Instead of repeatedly checking for updates, Gemini can notify you through Google Messages.

The integration can also help with everyday responsibilities. Gemini can send you reminders about upcoming subscription renewals, travel plans, and package deliveries, along with a daily briefing to help you stay on top of your schedule. Having all of this show up in an app you probably check several times a day makes a lot more sense than opening a separate AI app.

You can also use the conversation to ask Gemini regular questions or share photos and documents, so the integration isn’t exclusively limited to Tasks.

While Google has expanded Gemini Tasks to free users in the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, the Google Messages integration is currently only available in the US. You’ll also need to enable Tasks in the Gemini app before you can start receiving these messages.

TL;DR

• Motorola lists a December 8 shipping date for the Signature 27, while Best Buy shows December 11 deliveries or no stock.

• Motorola has confirmed that higher-than-expected demand is behind the revised shipping timelines.

• Some early buyers could still receive their phones ahead of the November 26 US retail launch.

A $1,600 Motorola phone proving harder to get hold of than expected isn’t something many would have predicted a year ago. Yet that’s the situation facing the Motorola Signature 27, the company’s big-ticket challenger to Samsung, Google, and Apple in the US. Demand has exceeded Motorola’s expectations, and new buyers may have to wait until December for their phones to arrive.

As spotted by 9to5Google, shipping dates for the Signature 27 have slipped into December. Motorola confirmed to the publication that demand has exceeded its initial expectations, resulting in revised shipping timelines for some orders.

We’re excited by the strong consumer response of the new motorola signature 27, with demand exceeding our initial expectations. As a result, some orders may experience updated shipping timelines. Our teams are working to meet demand and get devices to customers as quickly as possible.

Our own checks show that Motorola’s website currently lists a December 8 shipping date, while availability at Best Buy appears to vary by location. Some of us are seeing a December 11 shipping date with no in-store pickup option, while others can no longer pre-order the phone and are instead greeted with a “Notify Me” button.

However, not everyone is facing a longer wait. Some Signature 27 buyers are still on course to receive their units in time for the official retail launch. This suggests at least some early pre-orders are moving through the fulfillment process.

The Signature 27 was originally slated to go on sale in the US on November 26, following a week of pre-orders. Meanwhile, European sales began on November 16, and Motorola has now confirmed a December 9 launch in India.

What’s particularly interesting about the demand is that Motorola isn’t undercutting the competition this time. At $1,600, the Signature 27 is asking buyers to part with a serious chunk of change. Granted, a 7,000mAh battery, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, and 200MP telephoto camera make for a compelling hardware package. Motorola’s seven-year software support commitment, despite its caveats, also makes the asking price a little easier to stomach.

For years, Motorola’s biggest challenge in the US flagship market was giving people a reason to buy its phones over a Galaxy or Pixel. With the Signature 27, its immediate challenge appears to be getting enough phones into buyers’ hands.

HUAWEI found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets in the US

HUAWEI's latest guilty verdict could spell trouble for its smartphones well beyond the US.

•

•

•

Rita El Khoury / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Huawei has been found guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts in a US trial, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud, and sanctions violations.

• The verdict adds another hurdle for Huawei as it continues to face US restrictions that have kept its smartphones out of the mainstream American market since 2019.

Chinese smartphone maker HUAWEI makes some of the best Android smartphones in the world. However, the company hasn’t been allowed to sell its devices in the US since its 2019 ban, when the Trump administration added the company to the US Commerce Department’s Entity List. That decision had a major impact on HUAWEI’s smartphone business, with Google subsequently delivering it another blow by barring the company from using its services for new devices.

Now, HUAWEI is facing another setback in its already strained relationship with the US. A federal jury in Brooklyn has found the company guilty of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks, adding another complication to what was already looking like an uphill battle for its return to the American smartphone market.

Speaking with press before the Mate 90 launch earlier this year, HUAWEI’s Richard Yu had reportedly said that the company’s global phone share “was once number one,” but now, it only sell several million units of smartphones outside China every year. He had added that the company is “trying to return to the overseas market step by step.” However, this latest guilty verdict in the US could put a damper on HUAWEI’s global growth plans.

The jury found HUAWEI guilty on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank and wire fraud, and violations of US sanctions. Prosecutors accused the company of stealing intellectual property from American technology firms, including Cisco, Motorola, and T-Mobile, while also concealing business dealings in sanctioned countries such as Iran.

However, the jury acquitted the company of the more serious racketeering conspiracy charge and conspiracy to obstruct justice. HUAWEI has said it plans to appeal the convictions, but it could still end up facing billions of dollars in financial penalties during the sentencing.

In a statement issued after the verdict, Huawei wrote:

The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades. No court ever found HUAWEI liable for willful intellectual property misappropriation, and the company was never ordered to pay damages for trade secret misappropriation. We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests….HUAWEI takes its compliance obligations seriously. We remain focused on serving our customers and partners and ensuring continuous and stable business operations.

Google explains why your Nest camera is missing some features in the Home app

No, Google Home's limited Nest camera controls aren't a bug.

•

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

TL;DR

• Google is clearing up confusion around the Nest-to-Google Home transition, explaining why some users only see a live camera feed without the usual controls.

• Nest cameras and doorbells that haven’t been transferred to Google Home won’t have access to features like event history, timeline scrubbing, and notifications.

• Users can manually transfer their cameras now by tapping “Get started” in Google Home or wait for Google’s automatic migration on January 25, 2027.

Google is finally putting an end to the Nest app on January 25, 2027, moving supported Nest devices into Google Home. This migration is part of Google’s broader effort to bring its smart home ecosystem under one roof. However, it seems there’s been some confusion as to how the migration will work.

Since Google’s announcement about retiring the Nest app, users trying to move to the Google Home app noticed that their cameras and doorbells weren’t showing all the features they expected. Now, Google has explained why this is the case.

According to the company, Nest cameras and doorbells that haven’t been transferred to Google Home won’t have access to features like event history, timeline scrubbing, and notifications.

Anish Kattukaran, Google’s Senior Director of Product Management for Home and Nest, addressed the issue in a post on X, explaining that users who see a limited camera interface likely haven’t transferred their devices from the Nest app to Google Home yet.

Google

Kattukaran says users should tap the “Get started” prompt to move their cameras over and unlock the full experience. Alternatively, they can simply wait for Google to automatically transfer their devices on January 25, 2027.

The clarification follows similar advice shared by the Google Nest community on Reddit. According to the community post, if your Nest camera or doorbell in Google Home only shows a live video stream but doesn’t offer event history, timeline scrubbing, or notifications, your device hasn’t completed the migration.

In other words, seeing a live feed in Google Home doesn’t necessarily mean your camera has been fully transferred to the app. You’ll need to complete the migration to get access to the full set of camera controls and features.

If you don’t want to wait until January, Google has also published instructions for manually transferring Nest cameras and doorbells to Google Home.

items.summary: Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from the platform, with Tidal rejecting AI songs in the future. Tidal lead Robert Andersen said 43 percent of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days have been…
items.body: Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from the platform, with Tidal rejecting AI songs in the future. Tidal lead Robert Andersen said 43 percent of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days have been flagged as AI-generated. Approximately 29 million songs will be deleted and Tidal expects 80,000 to 85,000 songs to be rejected per day. AI music will start disappearing on December 9 and will be "completely gone" at the beginning of 2027. AI-assisted music will continue to be allowed, since the policy is only for songs made entirely with AI tools. Tidal previously demonetized AI music, but removing it goes a step further. Andersen said Tidal believes the move will "resonate with both artists and listeners alike" because 96 percent of AI songs get zero plays. Apple hasn't banned AI songs from Apple Music , but it introduced AI Transparency Tags earlier this year. Apple is relying on labels and distributors to disclose when AI has been used, and it said in August that tracks "materially generated using AI" must have a "Made With AI" label. In April, ‌Apple Music‌ VP Oliver Schusser said that more than a third of monthly uploads to ‌Apple Music‌ are 100 percent AI-generated, but AI music accounted for less than 0.5 percent of actual listening. items.body: Festivitas is a fun little holiday-themed Mac app that developer Simon Støvring introduced two years ago and has been updating since. Its main purpose is to add lights to the Mac's Dock and menu bar, but there's also a version for the iPhone and iPad . The holiday 2026 Festivitas update adds new customizations. For the first time, you can upload custom bulb shapes. There's an option to import an image and convert it to a bulb in a string of lights. Simple PNGs on a transparent background produce the best results, and for more complex images, bulbs can use the original colors. You can customize light shapes, color, size, opacity, drop height, cable thickness, and more in the Settings. Lights can animate with different patterns, like pulse, twinkle, chase, and wave. There are pointer decorations like sparkles, bubbles, falling leaves, confetti, a Christmas tree, a wreath, and more. Falling snow will now pile up on top of app windows for an added holiday effect. You can adjust snow rate, density, and flake size. Snow and lights can be displayed above app windows or just on the desktop, with lights also visible on the Dock. Shortcuts can be used to play music and turn on lights, activate the snow effect if the weather forecast includes snow, and start a snowstorm. Along with custom bulb shapes and falling snow, Festivitas for the iPhone and ‌iPad‌ now fully transparent animated widgets on the without a screenshot workaround. Festivitas for Mac requires some accessibility access to work. I asked Støvring about Apple's planned permission changes in macOS 27.3, and how they will affect the Festivitas app. He said Festivitas gets far more access than it needs because Apple's options aren't granular enough, and he'd prefer to ask for less access. Menu bar lights, snow, and pointer effects work without the System & App Protection Override permission, while lights in the Dock and snow landing on windows require access. items.title: Google Says Apple's iOS Browser Rules Offer 'Choice on Paper, Not in Practice'
items.summary: Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult. Mozilla recently joined a coalition of up to 55,000 businesses and organi…
items.body: Google's Chrome for Developers team today supported Mozilla's complaint about Apple's rules on non-WebKit browser engines in the European Union, calling out restrictions that make launching an alternative engine too difficult. Mozilla recently joined a coalition of up to 55,000 businesses and organizations to ask the European Commission to force Apple to change its browser rules. Apple started allowing alternative browser engines in the EU in early 2024 , but the coalition says no browser maker has been able to transfer its EU users from Apple's WebKit engine to a new engine because of Apple's conditions. Mozilla explained that using its Gecko browser engine instead of WebKit would require releasing a second Firefox app. Apple says apps with alternative browser engines have to be distributed only in the EU, so Mozilla has been unable to add Gecko to its existing app. Firefox users in the EU would need to transfer to a new app and move all their content, and many users might not be willing to switch. Mozilla said Apple's conditions are "unworkable" and that Apple has only complied with the EU's Digital Markets Act "on paper." Chrome for Developers echoed the statement in its X post: We agree with @mozilla. Nearly 3 years after alternative browser engines on iOS were EU-mandated, zero launched due to remaining Apple restrictions. Forcing browsers to ship separate apps and re-acquire users is choice on paper, not in practice. Though one Google team expressed support for Mozilla, Google did not sign the open letter to the European Commission. In 2023, Google started work on an experimental version of Chromium for iOS with the Blink engine, but Google said it was only a prototype that would not be released. In June 2025, Mozilla and Apple participated in a DMA workshop where Mozilla brought up iOS support for third-party browser engines.
